title: Tenant-scoped forwarding proxy for on-prem observability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight tenant-scoped forwarding proxy that runs inside customer VPCs / on-prem sites to centralize and normalize telemetry (traces, metrics, logs) before it crosses the network boundary to Redwood-hosted collectors. The proxy enforces tenant isolation, PII scrubbing rules, adaptive sampling, and per-tenant rate limits while preserving trace context for end-to-end latency analysis.
background: Dedicated and Private customers often run local collectors inside their network footprints. Current approaches either require customers to operate full-featured collectors or to open wide egress to multiple endpoints. We need a small-footprint, opinionated forwarding proxy that standardizes telemetry envelope, performs lightweight enrichment and scrubbing, and provides tenant-aware routing so the control plane can safely accept data from mixed environments without risking cross-tenant leakage.
goals: 1) Provide a single binary/container that customers can run on-prem or in VPCs to accept OTLP/HTTP inputs and forward to Redwood with tenant metadata. 2) Enforce tenant isolation (no mixing), PII redaction for configured fields, and sampling/rate controls. 3) Preserve trace/span context and add routing headers to support downstream routing and cost attribution. 4) Offer a simple config and health endpoints for operators and SREs.
non_goals: 1) This ticket does not implement a full collector pipeline (no heavy transforms or advanced enrichment). 2) No long-term storage or local buffering beyond short retry windows. 3) Not adding new SDK instrumentation changes at this stage.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts OTLP gRPC and OTLP HTTP traces/metrics and basic JSON logs from customers with minimal config
Per-tenant routing header is attached and validated; any payload without valid tenant header is rejected with 401/400 depending on config
Config-driven PII scrubbing applies to configured keys in trace attributes and log bodies and is verifiable in integration tests
Adaptive sampling rules can be configured per-tenant and reduce forwarded traces according to thresholds
Per-tenant egress rate limiting prevents single tenant from saturating egress link (configurable in requests/sec/bytes)
End-to-end trace id is preserved when forwarding; Redwood backplane dashboards show traces with correct tenant tag
Proxy exposes /health and /metrics and emits telemetry for its own resource usage (CPU/mem) and dropped/forwarded counts
Automated integration test runs against a Redwood staging collector showing correct routing and no cross-tenant leakage
design_notes:
- Implementation will be based on a minimal Rust binary using tonic for OTLP gRPC and hyper for HTTP inputs.
- Config format: YAML with explicit tenant mappings, scrubbing rules (regex based), sampling policies, and rate limits.
- Forwarding uses a secure mutual-TLS channel to Redwood ingress with per-tenant certs or a token envelope.
- Trace propagation: preserve traceparent/w3c headers and add 'x-redwood-tenant' header for control-plane routing.
- Local buffering: bounded ring buffer for short network outages (configurable by size/time).
- Admin endpoints: /metrics (Prometheus), /health, /config, and a /debug/last-scrubbed-sample (redacts sensitive fields) for SRE debugging.
implementation_steps: Prototype OTLP gRPC ingest server with pass-through forwarding (Luca) - 2d
Add HTTP ingest and JSON log normalization (Jordan) - 2d
Implement tenant header validation and rejection logic (Aisha) - 1d
PII scrubbing engine (regex-based) with unit tests and sample vectors (Data team + Security) - 3d
Adaptive sampling library integration and config mapping (Luca) - 2d
mTLS/token envelope implementation for secure egress (Infra) - 3d
Add Prometheus metrics and health endpoints, small docker image build pipeline (DevEx) - 2d
Write integration tests against staging collector that assert no cross-tenant leakage (QA) - 3d
Create Helm chart/compose example and README for customers (Solutions) - 2d
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Mis-scrubbing could drop critical debugging fields. Mitigation: Add per-tenant safelist and override with audit logging of samples (redacted) to console for 7 days.
Risk: Performance overhead at high throughput. Mitigation: Keep proxy single-threaded fast-path for pure pass-through and offload heavy scrubbing to worker pool with bounded queue.
Risk: Certificate management complexity for mTLS. Mitigation: Support token envelope fallback and provide a small cert rotation helper script.
Risk: Customers will expect full collector functionality. Mitigation: Document clear non-goals and provide migration path to full collector if needed.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scrubbing regex patterns with representative PII vectors
Load test with 10k spans/sec to validate sampling and rate limiting behavior
Integration test that sends traces from two tenants and asserts separation at Redwood ingress
Chaos test: simulate egress outage and verify bounded buffering and backpressure behaviors
SRE runbook validation: restore workflow for certificate rotation and token revocation
rollout_notes:
- Initial rollout as opt-in for Private customers in EU region.
- Feature gate on customer account enabling proxy acceptance; default off.
- Provide migration docs and example configs.
- Monitor dropped/forwarded counts and tenant error rates for first 72 hours after enablement.
- If >0.5% malformed or rejected envelopes across accounts, rollback and engage debugging runbook.
